title: Reader Poll: Welcome to The Valley of Ashes - Hudson River Blue
content: New York City FC — Reader Poll. # Reader Poll: Welcome to The Valley of Ashes. The results are in, and you voted to name New York City FC's new soccer stadium in Queens after a line from F. Hundreds of responses to our reader poll have left us with a clear New York City FC stadium nickname winner: The Valley of Ashes. NYCFC supporters look ready to reclaim and repurpose a phrase connected to the area’s polluted past, with 40.6% of the votes we received in favor of dubbing the shiny new soccer facility The Valley of Ashes. The “pigeon” nickname for New York City FC is always a point of contention and debate, but a good portion of our voters look ready to embrace the avian moniker when the team’s permanent home opens. See you at The Valley of Ashes when Pep Guardiola leads out his New York City FC side for their first match in the new stadium in 2027 (just kidding about Pep, but hey, you never know).

title: A celebration of Three Rivers Stadium, perfectly named and perfectly flawed - The Athletic
content: # A celebration of Three Rivers Stadium, perfectly named and perfectly flawed. Three Rivers Stadium had the perfect name. For all of its history — it was home to four Super Bowl champions, two World Series winners and even a Stanley Cup celebration — there were at least twice as many reasons Pittsburghers couldn’t wait to see it replaced. And that Pittsburgh thing where fans leave games early no matter the score, that started at Three Rivers Stadium. Its predecessor might not have been the equivalent of a mausoleum, because no mausoleum had sections that swayed like the ones wheeled into place for Steelers Sundays, but Three Rivers Stadium was a place where something truly unbelievable had to happen for it to become a lasting memory. It was one thing for each of the cities’ new stadiums to look like one another, but if either of the stadiums should have had “river” in its name, Pittsburgh’s should have been the one.

title: Same stadium, new name: Why World Cup venues are getting rebranded for the tournament
content: Arrowhead Stadium is undergoing a major transformation as Kansas City prepares to host six FIFA World Cup matches starting June 16. (AP) -- The stadiums that will host World Cup matches are removing all traces of their usual corporate sponsors in anticipation of the tournament that starts next week. At AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas, home of the NFL’s Dallas Cowboys, workers on Tuesday continued the process of covering the “AT&T” on the stadium’s facade. AT&T, and the other stadium sponsors at World Cup venues, are not FIFA sponsors, which are guaranteed exclusive rights during the tournament that runs through July 19. As a result, most of the 16 host stadiums are being rebranded with generic city names. Arrowhead Stadium will be Kansas City Stadium. title: Three Rivers Stadium (Pittsburgh) – Society for American Baseball Research
content: # Three Rivers Stadium (Pittsburgh). Three Rivers Stadium; if it wasn’t the most picturesque coliseum in American sports history, it was perhaps one of the most perfectly named. At the confluence of those two waterways, the point of the triangle, is formed the Ohio River; and it’s there, where the three rivers converge, across the Allegheny River from the Golden Triangle, on the riverbank known as the north shore, that Pittsburgh’s sports fans gathered for 31 years at Three Rivers Stadium to watch their favorite baseball team, the Pirates. In 1882 the Alleghenys,1 a founding member of the American Association, began play on the north shore at Exposition Park, in what would be the first incarnation of a structure known by that name. If the lineage of today’s Pittsburgh Pirates2 can be traced to that first Alleghenys team playing at the first Exposition Park on the north shore, then Opening Day 1891 marks the date when all of the attributes of one of baseball’s most historic franchises were finally in place.
